note: Classical muhurat rules, as commonly tabulated. Regional and sampradaya practice differs, and a family's own pandit is the final word. Nakshatra numbers are 0=Ashwini .. 26=Revati; tithis are 1..15 within each paksha.

functions.name: Wedding (Vivaha)
functions.note: Tuesday and Saturday are avoided. Rikta tithis (4, 9, 14), Ashtami, Purnima and Amavasya are avoided. The Nadi and Bhakoot doshas from Guna Milana are read alongside this, not instead of it.

functions.name: Engagement (Sagai)
functions.note: Read as a wedding without the stricter nakshatra list. Many families treat the engagement and the wedding as one muhurat and take a single date.

functions.name: Griha Pravesh
functions.note: Entering is traditionally done in the second half of the day, and the milk is boiled over at the threshold.

functions.name: Naming (Namkaran)
functions.note: Usually done on the eleventh day after birth, or on a later auspicious day. The name syllable is traditionally taken from the birth nakshatra pada.

functions.name: First rice (Annaprashan)
functions.note: Traditionally in the sixth or eighth month for a boy and the fifth or seventh for a girl, though families differ.

functions.name: Starting a business
functions.note: Often paired with a small Ganesha and Lakshmi puja, and with opening the books on the same day.

functions.name: Buying a vehicle
functions.note: Traditionally the vehicle is worshipped before it is driven - a lamp, kumkum, a coconut and a short prayer.

functions.name: Bhoomi pujan / foundation
functions.note: The first dig is traditionally done at an auspicious moment, with the ground worshipped first.
